title: The Friend at Midnight
reflectionText: The man inside rises because of the other man's persistence. Jesus then says: ask, seek, knock. He does not end with a promise that every desired outcome will be granted; he ends with the Father giving the Holy Spirit to those who ask him. The comparison moves from a reluctant friend to a Father who gives good gifts. Where have you stopped asking, seeking, or knocking?
editorialNotes: PAL Daily supervised production, Batch G completion pass. Luke 11:5-13 ONLY. Source category: PARABLE FOLLOWED BY DIRECT TEACHING, the teaching itself using parabolic imagery (11:11-12). The anchor is one coherent speech from Jesus — parable at 11:5-8, direct teaching at 11:9-13 — and remains one Traditional item; it was not split, reclassified, or given a new anchor or story key. Jesus supplies no allegorical interpretation of the parable, and none was invented. Retains the friend at midnight, the three loaves, the shut door and children in bed, importunity rather than friendship as the reason he rises (11:8), ask/seek/knock (11:9-10), the bread/fish/egg vs stone/serpent/scorpion comparisons (11:11-12), and the final movement to the Father giving the Holy Spirit (11:13). The Holy Spirit conclusion is NOT replaced with a generic 'every request granted' promise; no household scenery, sleeping arrangements, emotions, or later actions invented. primaryCharacterId 'jesus' per the parable pattern. Narrator VOICE_RUTH_COMFORT, mood encouraging (owner-locked). KJV LANE REPAIRED 2026-08-06 under ADR-031. The prior KJV text reproduced almost the whole anchor: 230 of 231 normalized tokens matched, in a single 229-token uninterrupted source run, the one unmatched token being the added name 'Jesus'. The mechanical reconstruction check returned false only because that speaker tag replaced 'And he said unto them', which is not evidence of retelling craft. The repair transformed the narrator and audience frame (Jesus speaks unto them, which the prior text dropped), Jesus' introduction of the hypothetical and the 11:5 scenario narration, the speech frames around the two parable characters, the 11:8 referents (the man within is the one who rises; the importunity belongs to him that asketh; the loaves are the object given), the audible 11:8 / 11:9 seam between parable conclusion and direct command, the father/son referents at 11:11, and the division of long biblical periods into spoken beats. Essential parable dialogue (the request at 11:5-6 and the refusal at 11:7) and the teaching of 11:9-13 are preserved exact or near-exact where the wording is itself the central action; 'importunity' is retained. No interpretation, new scene, application, moral, audience reaction, narrator summary, or material outside the anchor was added; Matthew 7 and other parallels were not consulted. The earlier note justified these lanes by word-count parity with the 235-word passage; that is not valid retelling evidence under ADR-031 and is withdrawn. Measured after repair: WEB 240 words (unchanged), KJV 245 words. shortScripture:true remains — owner-approved, padding to the 300-word floor is forbidden, and the untouched WEB lane is still below that floor.
